title: GCLI-12c: code-map time budget, enforcement and measurement, then ADR 0005 and README
description: Child of GCLI-12, split confirmed by the leader on 2026-11-17 after the worker's size read (the whole is well over the ~400-line ceiling). Builds to opum-doc DEC-216 (a4) and opum-cli's CodeMapProducer seam (opum-ai/opum-cli dev, src/context/code-map.ts, and ADR 0008), read by ref only. NOT STARTED: 12a's shape depends on opum-doc's ruling on port-versus-merge (Q1), pending. Slice c of three, after 12b: the time budget per DEC-216 (a4)(b). Measure the wall time of glyph code-map on opum-cli, lore-cli, quest-cli, glyph-cli and opum-desktop, cold and warm, at least 10 runs per repository and cache state, reporting p50, p95 and max per cell with the machine and the glyph commit, by running glyph read-only against them; propose budget = round-up(2 x worst p95) to the next 0.5 s to the leader for opum-doc, which fixes the number in the GCLI-12 record. Past the budget code-map returns what it has under omissions with reason time-budget, never runs past it and never returns nothing silently. ADR 0005 cites DEC-216 (a4) and the fixed number; the README records the seam and the budget.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The measurement is reported per repository and cache state with p50, p95, max, the machine and the glyph commit, and a budget proposal is sent for opum-doc to fix.
Past the budget, code-map returns the pointers it has with an omission whose reason is time-budget, finishes within the budget, and never returns an empty answer silently.
ADR 0005 cites DEC-216 (a4) and the number opum-doc fixed; the README names the seam and the budget.
Tests cover the time-budget omission; bun run check passes.

implementationNotes: Input for the time budget, from GCLI-40 (the 12a-1 pure layer): the producer's extractors are quadratic in a long unbroken token, because the pathsNamedIn pattern runs over the whole text. Measured with bun 1.3.14 on the worker's machine: about 13 ms per call at 5,000 characters, about 200 ms at 20,000 (the producer's own task-text bound), about 5 s at 100,000. collectIdentifiers calls pathsNamedIn again and the producer calls it once itself, so a hostile 20,000-character task text costs roughly 0.4 s before any git read. It is a cost, not pinned behaviour: a linear rewrite returns the same bytes. opum-cli is filing the defect upstream.

Carried from GCLI-37 close-out (non-blocking, fold in where GCLI-38 touches the files): (1) test/parity.test.ts hostile-config test: use a separate GLYPH_CACHE_DIR per run so the index build is compared across configs. (2) test/cli.test.ts cache-hit test: assert a cache .json exists after the miss so the second run is known to be a HIT. (3) src/codemap.ts ranking comment omits the symbol tier. Tier 3 landed at 678c5fd.

DEC-216 (a10), 2026-11-17, verbatim:
"BUDGET: 7.0 s. That is round-up(2 × the worst p95), quest-cli cold at 3.365 s, by (a4)(b)'s rule. glyph-cli's measurement (Apple M4, glyph d97958f1, 5 repositories × cold/warm × 10 runs) is the basis and goes into the GCLI-12 record and ADR 0005 verbatim, caveats included: n=10 so p95 is the nearest rank, the task texts are synthetic, opum-desktop's HEAD moved during its cell, and the GCLI-40 quadratic adds about 0.2–0.4 s at 20,000 characters. The constant is named. Changing it needs a new measurement and a new record, never an edit alone.

DESIGN: A, in-process.
- The budget is checked between units of work, and each git call is capped at the remaining time.
- The ONE named gap: a single synchronous index build can overrun on a repository far larger than the five measured. That overrun is reported as an `omissions` entry with reason `time-budget`, carrying the elapsed time, never silently.
- ADR 0005 names the gap, and the condition under which B (a killable subprocess build) would be reopened: a real repository whose cold build alone exceeds the budget.
- Proof: a unit-boundary check stops a slow fake unit and reports time-budget. A forced slow index build overruns and IS reported. Warm runs on the five repositories stay well under budget."

GCLI-38 measurement (basis of DEC-216 (a10)), 2026-11-17, Apple M4 / macOS 27.0.1, glyph d97958f1195311a6ed48bf3a9ceeeb2b7555bb40, `glyph code-map --source-ref HEAD` read-only against each checkout, 10 runs per cell, cold = empty cache per run, warm = one primed cache; seconds p50 / p95 / max. opum-cli (8b901ae) cold 1.429 / 1.636 / 1.636, warm 0.357 / 0.382 / 0.382. lore-cli (f3398b05) cold 2.085 / 2.439 / 2.439, warm 0.390 / 0.563 / 0.563. quest-cli (78492f2f) cold 2.914 / 3.365 / 3.365, warm 1.889 / 2.041 / 2.041. glyph-cli (d97958f) cold 0.485 / 0.531 / 0.531, warm 0.231 / 0.252 / 0.252. opum-desktop (2378d85 at the end of its cell, b634b2d at the start: its HEAD moved during the run) cold 0.919 / 1.273 / 1.273, warm 0.273 / 0.357 / 0.357. Caveats: n=10 so p95 is the nearest rank and equals the max; the task texts are synthetic (six exported names plus one source path); the GCLI-40 quadratic adds about 0.2 to 0.4 s at 20,000 characters. Worst p95 = quest-cli cold 3.365 s; 2 x 3.365 = 6.73; budget 7.0 s.

Warm re-measurement on the final build (DEC-216 (a10) proof clause "Warm runs on the five repositories stay well under budget"), 2026-11-17, Apple M4 / macOS 27.0.1, glyph a8c992a6768ee9bb76cd0c3e802a7ec209bcebd6, read-only, one uncounted priming run then 10 runs per repository, aborting on any code-map#time-budget row (none on any of 50 runs). Warm p50 / p95 / max seconds: opum-cli (8b901ae) 0.339 / 0.368 / 0.368; lore-cli (f3398b05) 0.349 / 0.359 / 0.359; quest-cli (78492f2f) 1.831 / 1.979 / 1.979; glyph-cli (a8c992a) 0.213 / 0.215 / 0.215; opum-desktop (2d87cf8, its HEAD moved again) 0.257 / 0.261 / 0.261. Worst warm p95 1.979 s = 28% of the 7.0 s budget. Same caveats: n=10, synthetic texts. Recorded as a dated addendum in ADR 0005.

Carried item N6 (from the PR 86 confirmatory review), verbatim: "the "budget already spent" test (timeBudgetMs: 0). Rev-parse now runs with a 1 ms timeout, so the stage is either "source ref" or "named paths" depending on timing. The test does not assert the stage, so it stays green. Pin it with `now: () => 0`, so the budget is spent before any read, if determinism matters there."

Carried item N7 (from the PR 86 confirmatory review), verbatim: "the exact mid-run pin is tied to how many times the code reads the clock (as M2 showed). Any added `now()` call will move it. A comment beside the pin would save the next editor a search." Both N6 and N7 are for the next PR that touches test/codemap-budget.test.ts.

Close-out. Landed as opum-ai/glyph-cli#86, squash e0807cdf7531d133195a32fa095285f8a7f254bf on dev (reviewed head c2135fe, Opus confirmatory APPROVE after round 1 REQUEST CHANGES at 3b5593a: B1 every git read under the budget, B2 signal deaths stay indeterminate, N1-N3). DEC-216 (a10) fixed the budget at 7.0 s and design A; ADR 0005 is Accepted. Carried: N6 and N7 above. Dev was not promoted.
finalSummary: Code-map time budget landed in opum-ai/glyph-cli#86 at e0807cd (budget 7.0 s per DEC-216 (a10); ADR 0005 Accepted). N6 and N7 carried in the close-out note.
